newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ciment Francais slams Bulgarian cement plant sale.
newsitem.headline: Ciment Francais slams Bulgarian cement plant sale.

text.p: French cement company Ciments Francais alleged "irregularities" in a plan to sell Bulgaria's Devnya cement production plant to a Bulgarian-Spanish investment consortium and asked the Bulgarian government to investigate.

"The lack of credibility of this offer is illustrated by the absence of financial details required by the initial criteria, the successive extensions of the negotiation period due to the consortium's inability to furnish bank guarantees, and the absence of a genuine business plan," Ciments Francais said in a statement.
Ciments Francais "thus judges it necessary to draw the Bulgarian government's attention to the anomalies and irregularities which have characterised the privatisation process".
Ciments Francais is a unit of Italcementi Group.
The executive board of Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency last week approved the purchase of 70 percent of Devnya Cement by Bulgarian-Spanish investment consortium Marvex for $44.5 million.
The consortium was set up for the privatisation deal and the Spanish side, led by Moltiracion De Graneles, holds 80 percent.
The remaining 20 percent is held by Bulgarian private company ELVA, which distributes Russian Lada cars in Bulgaria.
The deadline for signing the contract is May 5.
Marvex said it had pledged to invest $209.5 million in the plant over the next five years.
